source_refs.note: Topic 19.6 with Quick Check 19.5, answered (PDF 46-47). The book's empirical formula 'CH3CONH2' for ethanamide is corrected to C2H5NO. Which printed structure belongs to parts (a) and (c) is unclear on the page, so the answers name each structure. Answers need review.

blocks.text: A skeletal formula can be turned back into a molecular formula in three steps.

items: Count the carbon atoms and the other atoms (heteroatoms) shown in the skeleton.
Each line is a bond and each corner is a carbon atom; double lines are double bonds. Count one carbon at the end of each line unless another atom is shown there.
Add enough H atoms to each carbon to give it four bonds.

blocks.alt: Two skeletal formulae. (a) But-2-ene: a zigzag of three lines with the middle one double; the end carbons carry 3 H each and the two middle carbons 1 H each, giving C4H8 and empirical formula CH2. (b) Ethanamide: a line to a carbon bearing C=O and NH2; the end carbon carries 3 H and the carbonyl carbon none, giving C2H5NO, which is also its empirical formula.
blocks.caption: Counting the atoms in two skeletal formulae (original diagram after the book's worked example).
blocks.long_description: In but-2-ene the two end carbons each need three hydrogens and the two carbons of the double bond one each, so the formula is C4H8; dividing by 4 gives the empirical formula CH2. In ethanamide the methyl carbon has three hydrogens, the carbonyl carbon none and the NH2 group two, so the formula is C2H5NO, which cannot be simplified.

items: Give the molecular formulae of the bond-line structures Br-CH2-CH2-COOH and the cyclohexane ring bearing a methyl and a prop-1-enyl group on the same carbon.
Give the molecular formulae of the dichlorocyclohexane and of the benzene ring carrying CH2Cl and CO2H groups.
